text:
mike.sales: Hey team — ACME (enterprise) is asking for a reserved capacity deal + a small buffer of credits for burst overages. They want predictable monthly cost but ability to absorb spikes without service drop. Can product confirm how we should handle pricing/credits and what to include in the SOW?
tara.support: They reported a couple of incidents last month where traffic spiked 3x for ~3 hours. Support suggested a temporary credit bucket rather than immediate throttling.
anya.product: Thanks — need to surface options quickly. Two high-level approaches: 1) Include N tokens/month as rollover credits + overage at per-token rate; 2) Soft cap with auto-burst and true-up billing (invoice the extra at month end). Both require billing + legal changes. Thoughts?
devon.eng: For runtime, soft burst is fine but we should limit sustained bursts to avoid hurting other tenants. Autoscale + fallback model variant ok. Need a flag to mark customer as "burst-allowed" in routing so we can enforce caps in 1-hr windows.
kevin.finance: From finance perspective we prefer explicit credits + clear overage rate. True-up introduces invoicing complexity and longer receivable cycles. Example numbers to consider: base reserved: $60,000/mo for 8-GPU pool, included credits: 2,000,000 tokens, overage: $0.0006/token (so 1M extra tokens = $600). We can model tiered overage if they want discount schedule.
mike.sales: ACME is ok with simple model as long as there's a buffer they can rely on without service interruption. They asked for rollover of unused credits and a one-time grace for first month.
anya.product: Proposal (quick): - Offer reserved capacity price as-is - Include 2M monthly credits, unused credits rollover up to 3 months - Overages billed at $0.0006/token with warning alerts at 70/90/100% - One-time first-month grace of 500k tokens (no charge) - Add a runtime flag to allow bursts subject to 1-hr sustained cap.
kevin.finance: That works but cap the rollover to avoid long tail exposure. 3 months is fine. Need a contract clause for termination true-up.
devon.eng: Implementation asks: 1) routing flag + enforcement window, 2) metrics to track credit consumption in near real-time, 3) a billing export that maps tokens -> billing lines. Engineering estimate: ~2.5 dev-weeks + QA for flag + telemetry, +1 week for billing export.
tara.support: I'll add a triage note and capture examples of last month spikes. Also need a playbook for when customer hits 100% and wants immediate additional capacity.
anya.product: Launch criteria (must-haves): legal signoff on SOW language; billing pipeline supports credit buckets and overage lines; console shows credit balance + alerts; runtime flag toggled for customer; support runbook. Nice-to-have: automated apply for grace in first invoice.
mike.sales: Timeline request from ACME: they'd like pilot in ~3 weeks. Can we do an opt-in pilot while we finalize contract?
devon.eng: Pilot mode (limit scope) = enable runtime flag + temporary manual billing offset. We can spin up pilot in ~2 weeks if legal ok with provisional SOW.
kevin.finance: Finance/Legal need to review numbers and contract language — route to legal now.
anya.product: OK — next steps: 1) tara.support to create support case with spike logs (PD-8910), 2) kevin to prepare provisional pricing sheet for legal, 3) devon to scope minimal pilot work and ETA, 4) anya to write SOW draft. I'll open a backlog ticket PD-4572 to track feature work + launch criteria.
tara.support: Created support case PD-8910 and attached logs.
ops-bot: Deploy bot: created ticket PD-4572 assigned to anya.product, devon.eng, kevin.finance.
mike.sales: Thanks — I'll update ACME that product is aligning on pilot + provisional SOW.
anya.product: If no objections by EOD I'll circulate SOW draft for review and lock pilot dates. :thumbsup:
